title: Batched upserts with ON CONFLICT must dedupe conflict keys before the statement
answers: PostgreSQL CardinalityViolation ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE command cannot affect row a second time
saving logged model tags with a repeated key fails on Postgres
duplicate tag key in one set_logged_model_tags call errors only on PostgreSQL
bulk upsert duplicate key last value wins
body:
Symptom: Logging logged-model tags with the same key twice in one call fails on PostgreSQL with "ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE command cannot affect row a second time". SQLite and MySQL accept it, and the old per-tag loop kept the last value.
Root cause: mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py:SqlAlchemyStore.set_logged_model_tags passed one row per input tag to _bulk_upsert. A repeated (model_id, tag_key) pair put two rows on the same conflict target in one INSERT ... ON CONFLICT statement.
Fix pattern: Dedupe rows by conflict key before calling _bulk_upsert, e.g. deduped = {tag.key: tag.value for tag in tags}, so the last value wins as session.merge did.
Constraints: Applies to any _bulk_upsert caller whose input can repeat a conflict-key value (ON CONFLICT on SQLite/PostgreSQL, ON DUPLICATE KEY on MySQL). Dedupe in the store rather than relying on caller order. The regression case is the repeated "dup" key in test_set_logged_model_tags_bulk_upsert.
Applies: Any new or changed caller of _bulk_upsert in mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py, including logged model tags.
applies: SQLAlchemy tracking store bulk upserts that write rows keyed by a composite primary key.
says: Saving multiple tags with the same key on a logged model fails in Postgres.
Updating model metadata crashes when the tag list contains duplicate label names.
Overwriting an existing model tag key in a batch should keep the newest value.
Bulk tagging a logged model throws a database conflict error on repeated attributes.
Editing model tags should let the latest duplicate entry override earlier entries cleanly.
search: Bulk upserts in the SQLAlchemy tracking store must deduplicate input rows by conflict key so the last value wins without triggering PostgreSQL cardinality errors. In mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py, SqlAlchemyStore.set_logged_model_tags passes rows to _bulk_upsert, where duplicate (model_id, tag_key) pairs cause ON CONFLICT failures. The store must perform deduplication internally rather than relying on caller order for any _bulk_upsert caller with composite primary keys, verified by test_set_logged_model_tags_bulk_upsert in tests/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store/test_sqlalchemy_store_runs.py.
